law_record.title: Blind persons (B)
law_record.text: Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind, or any driver of any vehicle who approaches or comes in contact with a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person with wisdom, shall immediately come to a full stop and take such precautions before proceeding as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind.

activation_conditions: a person wholly or partially blind is carrying a white or white-tipped-red cane, or is being assisted
the subject — a driver, or a pedestrian who is not blind — approaches or comes in contact with them
residue: blindness is inferred from the cane or the assistance, which is what the rule itself names
'such precautions as may be necessary' is a judgement element
summary.subject: driver

timing_requirements.requirement: 'immediately come to a full stop' — the halt must follow the observation without delay; both the reaction interval and the halt itself need declared bounds
the precautions must be taken before proceeding, so the stop persists until the conflict is resolved
